title: Hamiltonian-Preserving Symplectic Neural Networks for Robust Phase Retrieval in 4D STEM Ptychography
content: Four dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) has revolutionized structural characterization by capturing complete scattering distributions at each probe position [1]. While ptychographic reconstruction provides exceptional phase contrast, existing algorithms face challenges such as noise sensitivity, convergence instability, and multiple scattering artifacts [2,3]. These limitations stem from the inability to preserve the physical structure of electron wave propagation during reconstruction. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to ptychographic phase retrieval based on Hamiltonian mechanics. By recognizing that the evolution of the electron wave through the specimen follows Hamilton’s equations - with the probe wave function ψ(r) and specimen transmission function φ(r) acting as conjugate variables in an extended phase space - we develop a Symplectic Neural Network (SNN) [4]. The SNN architecture preserves the geometric structure of the Hamiltonian system through symplectic integration layers while learning complex electron-specimen interactions via modified potentials:
